Keep the service entirely in Python, but move provider parsing into a dedicated HTTP adapter and replace raw upstream errors with stable, sanitized service errors.

- **Aligned — Python only.** Mytech prefers application-specific HTTP adapters in the consuming application’s language. External HTTP alone does not justify another runtime. The project constraint therefore agrees with the [HTTP language guidance](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/external-http/rust-for-external-http-protocols.md); no deviation is needed.
- **Gap — parsing inside route handlers.** Give the provider integration its own boundary: decode and validate responses once, then translate them into project-owned values. Routes should coordinate application operations and translate their results into HTTP responses. Keep deterministic report transformations in pure functions. A small module is sufficient; this does not require a plugin system or interface around every dependency. See [boundaries and pure cores](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/boundary-owned-contracts-and-pure-cores.md).
- **Gap — returning upstream error strings.** Map provider failures to stable service-owned categories and sanitized messages. Callers should use categories for recovery rather than parse provider text. The adapter should also own timeout, retry, and resource policies. See [HTTP contracts and clients](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/architecture/external-http/external-http-contracts-and-handwritten-clients.md).

For this application-local integration, executable schemas plus independent provider examples may be sufficient; OpenAPI is not automatically required. The description does not establish schema validation, transport policies, or provider conformance evidence, so those remain **unknown**, rather than proven defects. Provider readiness likewise cannot be established from the proposal alone. See [provider qualification](/Users/sejunpark/IT/mytech/practices/external-provider-qualification.md).
